newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt ends up in late day rally,await CPI.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt ends up in late day rally,await CPI.

text.p: Emerging debt prices ended higher boosted by some short-covering and an improved tone in the U.S. Treasury and stock markets as players gear up for a new batch of key U.S. economic data, traders said.
Spreads were seen tighter by about five to 10 basis points across the board, traders said.
"Emerging debt prices ended the trading day slightly above where we closed on Friday," said one Brady trader. "We saw a late afternoon rally driven by short-covering and the recovery in the Dow."
U.S. stocks traded off 30 points earlier in the day but later recouped losses to end the day up 60 points.
The dollar was also strong and bonds were generally better bid, the Brady trader said. "At the end of the day some players who were short were trying to square up ahead of tomorrow's number."
In the U.S. Treasury market the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond closed off 1/32 at 93-10/32 to yield 7.17 percent.

Emerging debt prices recouped some losses after Friday's sharp selloff in the U.S. Treasury and stock markets, triggered by a stronger-than-expected U.S. wholesale inflation report that dragged down prices.

"We had had an exaggerated fall last week after the PPI numbers," said Thomas Trebat, head of emerging market research at Citicorp Securities. "Upon reflection we thought the market would probably think twice today and that seems to basically be what's happenend late this afternoon."

"Our market continues to be in a nutshell...very closely tied to broader investor sentiment about the U.S. market," Trebat said. "It is not really moving very much in terms of domestic fundamentals in either Latin America or in Eastern Europe."
"In both those parts of the world fundamentals are either neutral to positive, so what's dominating here is investor sentiment about the securities markets more broadly," Trebat said.

Meanwhile, concerns that a strong inflation report might prompt the Federal Reserve to hike interest rates again will keep players focused on Tuesday's key release of the U.S. consumer price index (CPI), which measures inflation at the consumer level.
The data is due out on Tuesday at 0830 EST/1230 GMT.
In a Reuter poll, U.S. economists predict a 0.2 percent rise in CPI. Excluding food and energy, the rate is expected to rise 0.3 percent.
"We have a rough week ahead of us," Trebat said. "Whether or not the market likes the CPI number I think that we'll be in a pattern of the market holding its breath day by day."

"This particular week I don't think there will be any permanent relief, Trebat added. "We'll see a seesaw week with prices in emerging debt stuck in a range below their peaks earlier in the year, but not weakening any further with respect to the Treasury market."
Among emerging debt issues, at 1730 EDT/2130 GMT, Argentine pars were up 3/8 at 61-1/8 bid whereas its FRBs were up 3/8 at 89 bid. Venezuela pars gained 1/2 to 68-5/8 bid.
Mexican pars gained 1/2 to 69-3/4 bid, Brazil C were up 1/4 at 73-3/4 bid.
Among Eastern European credits, Bulgaria IAB rose 3/8 to 57-3/8 bid, while Russian VN US$ was off 5/8 to trade at 76 bid.
